doc.title: Schuller Gunther — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Not allowed into jazz clubs until Cincinnati
summary: His parents forbade jazz clubs and Harlem; he first went freely at 17 in Cincinnati, where he met Ellington.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: I’d love to do that. I’d love to find out where and when you first heard the music live, and how that affected you, and the relationships that were formed from that.

That’s a good question, because I knew there were all these clubs in New York, because, as I say, a lot of broadcasts came from there. But I was not allowed to go at age 14 or 15. I was not able to go to any jazz club. My parents just would not tolerate that, especially to go to Harlem. They were fairly prejudicial about that. I wasn’t able to go anywhere until I went to Cincinnati at age 17 as principal horn, and then I was on my own. That’s by the way – I met Ellington, and we became very close friends.
